newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTHERN AFRICA SEEN HURT BY EU BEEF EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SOUTHERN AFRICA SEEN HURT BY EU BEEF EXPORTS.

text.p: Southern Africa's beef industry is being threatened by the continued subsidisation of export meat by the European Union, a grouping of southern African meat producers said on Thursday.

The Southern African Meat Producers Liaison Committee (SAMPLC) representing Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe, said in a statement EU beef was entering the South African market at a hefty discount to local wholesale prices.
"The consequent loss of potential earnings amounting to hundreds of millions of rand is having serious implications for beef producers in South Africa and the southern African region," SAMPLC said.

It said this showed a lack of coherence in EU policy whereby agricultural policy was undermining the European grouping's development cooperation aim. The EU development council is due to meet in the Netherlands on Friday to discuss the coherence of EU policies, SAMPLC said.

It said the volume of EU beef entering South Africa had increased dramatically since mid-1994, weighing on the country's fully developed industry and its role as a major market for beef-producing states in the region.
The damage caused to southern Africa far outweighed the benefits from European business, it said.

"In both South African and Namibia the income losses to the beef producers resulting from the increased volumes of subsidised exports, have exceeded the annual volume of EU development assistance transfers," the producers said.

South Africa had already requested that EU exports be reclassified so that they no longer qualify for refunds, but no measures have yet been taken by the European Commission despite them being aware of the problems.

The regional meat body said it had appealed to the EU to reclassify South Africa alongside its neighbouring countries so that it could also be eligible for export restitution payments for beef exports.
